newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bank robber kills self, ends hostage drama.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bank robber kills self, ends hostage drama.

text.p: A Mexican bank robber holding two hostages at gunpoint shot and killed himself on Monday upon finally realising he was hopelessly surrounded by police, a top Mexico City law official said.
The tense hostage standoff lasted more than five hours, with some of its more dramatic moments broadcast live on television.

"None of the police agents fired," Mariano Herran, deputy attorney general for Mexico City, told the television news programme 24 Hours, contradicting earlier reports from officers on the scene that police shot the man dead.
An autopsy photo was provided to 24 Hours to support Herran's claim.

Minutes before his death the robber, who answered to the name Gerardo and wore a white baseball cap pulled low over his face, came to the door of the bank holding the two hostages at gunpoint, waiving a pair of pistols at police, the hostages and reporters gathered outside the bank.
Herran said the unidentified robber, still holding two hostages at gunpoint, shot himself in the head after he and his victims entered the back seat of an escape car that the robber had demanded.
Confusion at the scene reined after the three entered the car, surrounded by police, and then shots rang out. Witnesses reported hearing two or three shots.

The holdup at a Bancomer branch in eastern Mexico City began earlier on Monday with a brief shootout that injured one police officer and one civilian. After the shootout, about a dozen hostages were released.
The Mexican government news agency Notimex said one officer was injured in the hand and a civilian was shot in the leg during the brief shootout as police arrived at the start of the robbery.
